conventions.convention: The controlled Hamiltonian is H − εh(t)B; Heisenberg evolution is α_t(A)=exp(itH/ℏ)Aexp(−itH/ℏ). Consequently the response kernel is +i Tr(σ[α_t(A),B])/ℏ.
The initial Gibbs density remains fixed as ε varies. The dynamical first variation does not differentiate a re-prepared Gibbs family.

The correlation Fourier convention is S(ω)=∫ exp(iωt)C(t)dt. Frequencies are angular frequencies (E_j−E_i)/ℏ. Spectral measures have atomic masses with observable-product units; their distributional densities have an additional factor of seconds.
Detailed balance uses reflection pushforward: S_AA(−dω)=exp(−βℏω)S_AA(dω). The coth fluctuation-response identity applies only away from zero; the zero-frequency correlation atom remains separate.
Infinite-dimensional normal-state response pairs trace-class densities only with bounded observables, assumes full Choice for the spectral group, and requires no energy or entropy moments.
Strong Schrödinger realization requires B(D(H))⊆D(H) and a bounded extension of [H,B]. The graph norm is ||ψ||+||Hψ||/E₀ for a fixed positive reference energy E₀.
The infinite-spin algebra is a norm completion, with Countable Choice retained. Its state is an invariant extension of consistent local densities; no global trace Hamiltonian is selected.
The Green–Kubo variance limit requires absolute integrability on [0,∞) of the specified real symmetrized covariance. Finite-range spatial interactions alone do not supply this hypothesis.
Cesaro dephasing retains entire equal-energy blocks, including coherences inside degenerate eigenspaces; it asserts averaged convergence, not pointwise relaxation.
Preparation, unitary dynamics and Born expectations are adopted physical assumptions. The prepared-response theorem is a conditional prediction with no empirical premises or apparatus validation.

load_bearing.statement: For a complex Banach space X, T>0, strongly continuous K:[0,T]→B(X), and continuous nonnegative a with ||K(t)||≤a(t), the recursively defined Volterra series converges uniformly for every complex ε and uniquely solves x′=εK(t)x, x(0)=x₀. With c_T=∫₀ᵀa(s)ds, its remainder after the linear term is at most ||x₀||(|ε|c_T)²exp(|ε|c_T)/2. Its stated skew-adjoint C-star and Hilbert-space cases give unitary solutions for real ε.

For finite dimension d≥1, Hermitian H,A,B, ℏ>0, β>0, fixed initial Gibbs density σ=exp(−βH)/Z, continuous real h on finite [0,T], and real ε, the unitary control H−εh(t)B has expectation Tr(σα_t(A))+ε∫₀ᵗh(s)R_AB(t−s)ds+r_ε(t), where R_AB(u)=i Tr(σ[α_u(A),B])/ℏ and |r_ε(t)|≤||A||(|ε|C_T)²exp(|ε|C_T)/2, C_T=(2/ℏ)∫₀ᵀ|h(s)| ||B||ds.

Assume Choice, a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, densely defined self-adjoint H, ℏ>0, a positive trace-class density ρ commuting with U₀(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ), bounded self-adjoint A,B, continuous real h on finite [0,T], and real ε. The trace-class interaction-picture equation ρ_I′=iεh(t)[B_t,ρ_I]/ℏ has the stated convolution response with kernel i Tr(ρ[α_u(A),B])/ℏ and remainder at most ||A||(|ε|C_T)²exp(|ε|C_T)/2.

Assume Choice, nonzero separable Hilbert space, densely defined self-adjoint K bounded below, and exp(−sK) trace class throughout an open positive interval containing β. For bounded A,B, the Gibbs correlation has the absolutely and uniformly convergent series ∑ᵢⱼrᵢAᵢⱼBⱼᵢexp(−iωⱼᵢt), with ∑ᵢⱼrᵢ|Aᵢⱼ||Bⱼᵢ|≤||A||||B||. Its atomic spectral measure is finite with total variation at most 2π||A||||B||.

For a unital complex C-star algebra, a point-norm continuous automorphism group, a bounded normalized positive invariant functional φ, centered self-adjoint V₁,…,V_m, and T>0, put X_a,T=∫₀ᵀα_t(V_a)dt and G_ab(s)=(Re φ(V_aα_s(V_b))+Re φ(V_bα_s(V_a)))/2. Then Re φ(X_a,TX_b,T)/(2T)=∫₀ᵀ(1−s/T)G_ab(s)ds, and this real symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite.

For finite dimension d≥1, Hermitian H and ℏ>0, U(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ) is a unitary group, its conjugations form matrix star-automorphisms, Schrödinger and Heisenberg trace expectations agree, and unitary evolution preserves finite von Neumann entropy. For β>0, the normalized Gibbs matrix is stationary and has the stated entire, strip-bounded KMS correlation.

concerns.concern: The Example calls B a 'bounded projection between the first two oscillator levels'. B is a bounded transition operator, not a projection: B²=b₀²(P₀+P₁), whereas B has off-diagonal entries and is not idempotent for the stipulated nonzero b₀. The calculations use the correct transition operator; the wording should identify a projected transition rather than call B a projection.

seams_checked.note: The algebraic Kubo theorem retains Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C-star condition, finite-range interaction hypotheses and the actual completed quasi-local algebra. Its use of the supplier's continuous isometric automorphism group is faithful; invariance of the state is imposed separately. No global Hamiltonian or temporal decay is inferred.

The reduced-unitary theorem cites finite-unitary only for unitarity of exp(−itH_tot/ℏ) for a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian. Its product-preparation channel conclusion is proved separately and does not infer a semigroup or bath limit. The citing text explicitly identifies the response supplier as draft.

The finite-response-redshift theorem applies finite Kubo to the same normalized cell Gibbs density and continuous finite-time controls. The change τ=Nt gives control Nh(Nt), kernel R_loc(Nt), and the same remainder constant. Spectral pushforward preserves atomic weights and the separate zero atom; the coth identity remains restricted to nonzero frequency. Static re-preparation is handled by its separate supplier.
